passage:
The city installed phone charging stations in subway stations. Travelers could charge their phones for free while waiting.
The stations were useful, but a warning sign was added: "Do not leave your phone alone." Some people had already forgotten phones or had them taken.
A teenager saw a phone left at a station. He gave it to station staff instead of ignoring it.
The staff said public tools work only when people use them responsibly.
The charging station solved one modern problem: dead batteries. But it also created old problems: carelessness, trust, and honesty.
Technology changes objects, but human behavior remains part of every system.
